Visiting Berth Gallery #101 The gallery runs the length of the visiting berths: a strip of armourglass on one side, a rail of chipped yellow paint on the other that marks the public viewing line, and a deck plate that hums with the pumps two floors down. Beyond the glass the cradles sit in hard floodlight, a Dray's blunt hull webbed with reaction-mass hoses, umbilicals slack on the deck, and past the last cradle the dark where the working berths go on out of sight. The air is cold and carries the ozone of cycled locks.
